title: Senior Frontend Engineer
summary: Own the component library that three product teams build on. You will spend more time deleting code than writing it.
description:
We are looking for a senior frontend engineer to take ownership of Northwind's shared component library. The role is equal parts API design and diplomacy: three product teams depend on these components, and every change is a negotiation.

You will work closely with design on tokens and theming, drive accessibility to WCAG 2.2 AA across the library, and maintain the migration path as we finish the move off our legacy stack.

title: Developer Experience Engineer
summary: Make the inner loop fast. Our test suite takes 22 minutes and everyone has opinions about it.
description:
Ravenline's platform team is hiring a DX engineer to own build, test and release tooling for a 40-engineer organisation.

Concretely: our CI takes 22 minutes and our local dev setup takes a new hire most of a day. Both numbers are yours to fix. You will have full autonomy over the toolchain and a mandate to remove things.

title: Security Engineer, Product
summary: Threat-model AI agent integrations before they ship, not after the incident review.
description:
Halden is embedding AI agents across its product surface, and we want a security engineer involved from the design stage rather than the postmortem.

You will threat-model agent-facing APIs, define what an agent is and is not allowed to do on a user's behalf, and build the guardrails that enforce it. Experience with capability-based authorization or human-in-the-loop approval flows is a strong signal.

title: Staff Engineer, Platform
summary: Ingest pipeline moves 4TB a day and falls over roughly once a quarter. Make it boring.
description:
Corvid's ingest pipeline handles about 4TB of event data daily. It works, but it has a quarterly failure mode nobody has had time to chase down properly.

We want a staff engineer to own reliability end to end: instrument it, find the real cause, and make the fix that stops it recurring. This is a role for someone who enjoys making systems unremarkable.

title: Product Designer (Systems)
summary: Design the primitives, not the screens. Partner directly with the component library team.
description:
A systems-minded product designer to work alongside our frontend platform team on tokens, primitives and documentation.

You will not be shipping feature screens. You will be defining the spacing scale everyone argues about, and then defending it. Accessibility is a requirement, not a phase.

title: Backend Engineer, Payments
summary: Money movement, idempotency and reconciliation. Correctness beats cleverness here.
description:
Solvent processes payouts for marketplaces. You will work on the ledger and reconciliation services, where every operation must be idempotent and every discrepancy must be explainable.

We care a great deal about test coverage on money paths and very little about framework fashion.
